title: Prefill transition standup — Oct 2025 field notes
content:
Meeting: informal standup / lab sync — prefill transition and batching adjustments
Date: 2025-10-21 — notes captured during late lab window (21:00-22:00 PT)
Attendees: Aisha, Marcus, Leah, Diego (brief joins from SRE)
Context: we are phasing the old prefill coordinator into the new zero-copy prefill bridge (goal: reduce duplicate KV materialization, cut cold-start latency for long-context requests). This week was focused on two things: (1) experiments to safely split prefill vs request-time work, and (2) heuristics for batch-splitting when there is a mix of short chat and long completion traffic.

Summary bullets (quick):
- Zero-copy snapshotting prototype validated on single-node perf rig: ~12% median P95 token latency improvement for 2–4k seqs when prefill applied ahead of time.
- Observed an unexpected 8% increase in memory churn on high-concurrency workloads due to short-lived KV references — need GC/eviction tuning.
- Batch-splitting rule "max-merge-age=25ms" reduced tail jitter but increased compute fragmentation; new heuristic proposed: dynamic max-merge-age based on observed coalescence.
- Night-ops run uncovered a regression in fallback routing: when prefill failed, fallback was retrying to same kernel variant, causing requeue storms. Patch in PR 718 blocks that loop.

Detailed notes / experiment logs:
- Zero-copy prefill run (Marcus)
  - Setup: single A100 node with perf workload simulating 30% long (>=3k tokens) + 70% short (<=512 tokens) requests. Prefill bridge precomputes key-value tensors and exposes read-only refs to runtime.
  - Result: median token generation latency improved ~12% at 95th percentile for long requests; throughput stable. Prefill memory overhead dropped vs previous prefill (no materialized duplicates) but transient pointer churn increased.
  - Action: add lightweight refcount sampling probe to measure pointer lifetimes (Diego).

- Batch-splitting heuristic experiments (Leah)
  - Baseline: static split by request length threshold (>=1024 -> long pool). Issues: bursty short traffic starved long-pool batching opportunities.
  - New approach: adaptive split using short/long queue occupancy + max-merge-age. When short pool >= X% of total, temporarily relax max-merge-age to allow more coalescing of mid-length requests.
  - Observed: tail latency for mids improved but average token cost increased by ~3%. Need to quantify cost/latency tradeoff on production-like traces.
  - Open: choose X (occupancy threshold) via cost-weighted objective. Proposal: simulate with last 7 days of traffic snapshots.

- Fallback/routing regression (night-ops)
  - Symptom: when prefill bridge throws a transient error (OOM spike), fallback routing tried same model variant repeatedly, queued a flood of retries to the same kernel. Resulted in short-lived queue pileups and error spikes.
  - Diagnosis: routing policy lacked backoff and variant-rotation on prefill failure path.
  - Fix: short-term patch in PR 718 — add exponential backoff + rotate to a compatible variant after 2 failures. Noted potential downstream: slightly higher cold-starts for those rotated variants.

Metrics and quick numbers observed (lab):
- Prefill zero-copy: P95 token latency for long reqs 340ms -> 299ms (12% improvement)
- Memory churn (GC events/sec) up 8% under 200-concurrency stress
- Batch size distribution: mean 28 tokens, median 14, with new merge-age=25ms we saw 5% increase in mean batch size for mid-length requests

Blockers / unknowns:
- GC/eviction: pointer churn suggests our current KV eviction hooks are touching too many objects; need SRE/infra input on safer weakref patterns. Blocker ticket: SERV-4521.
- Telemetry: we currently do not capture per-request refcount lifetimes; adding this probe risks overhead — we need an opt-in low-sample rate.
- Production simulation data: Leah needs last-7-days traffic snapshots for realistic cost/latency tradeoff sims. Request to infra: generate anonymized snapshot (JIRA: SERV-4569).

Decisions made in-sync:
- Move forward with zero-copy prefill prototype to on-prem staging for broader QA. Timeline: canary on 10/29 if infra snapshot and GC mitigations are in place.
- Merge-age heuristic: roll experimental adaptive merge-age behind runtime flag; default keep conservative 15ms in prod.
- Emergency backoff: keep PR 718 hotfix and schedule follow-up to implement a more principled routing-state machine (Spike assigned to Marcus).

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Diego: implement refcount sampling probe (low-rate sampling) + microbenchmark it — due 2025-10-24.
- Leah: run cost/latency sims on 7-day snapshot, produce chart and recommendation for X threshold — due 2025-10-27. Linked artifact: JIRA SERV-4569.
- Marcus: complete routing-state spike & write acceptance criteria for variant-rotation behavior — due 2025-10-30.
- Aisha: coordinate on-prem staging setup and get sign-off from infra for canary window 10/29 — due 2025-10-25.
- SRE (requested): review weakref + eviction behavior, propose GC tuning knobs we can expose — requested response by 2025-10-24.

Notes to self / ephemeral ideas:
- Consider a cheap bloom filter that indicates "recently touched" KV shards to avoid touching many objects on eviction path. Might reduce churn without full refcount changes.
- If adaptive merge-age increases cost too much, consider hybrid: aggressive coalescing in dedicated long-worker pools only.
- Could attach a small per-request "prefill hint" score so routing can prefer prefill-optimized kernels for requests above threshold — cheap to compute at edge.

Risks flagged:
- Memory churn could trigger eviction storms on multi-tenant nodes; must gate rollout behind SRE sign-off.
- Backoff + variant-rotation could create oscillation if not smoothed; need hysteresis.

Next sync: quick midweek check (20–30 minute) Friday 2025-10-24 morning; full lab window next Tuesday 2025-10-28 18:00 PT for canary dry-run.

Random fragments captured during sync (informal):
- "If we can keep prefill bridge read-only and snapshottable, that's half the battle." — Leah
- "Sampling is our friend — but keep it cheap." — Marcus
- "We should write a playbook for prefill fallback; ops oncall shouldn't be surprised by rotating variants." — Diego

End of notes.
